reason: The text explicitly states that God heard the cry of the Hebrew people (צַעֲקַת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּאָה אֵלַי - 'the cry of the children of Israel has come to me'), indicating they are actively expressing their suffering and concerns. God responds positively to this expression by commissioning Moses to liberate them from Egypt. Rather than discouraging expression, the passage validates the Hebrews' vocal complaints about Egyptian oppression.
